correctness.rationale: From the exact nodewise equation of arXiv:2607.05608, connectedness rules out mixed zero/positive equilibrium support and identical neighbor sets enforce exactly two positive class values. The strictly increasing F_d(s)=s^(d+1)/(1-s) reduces all equilibria to the smooth one-parameter curve lambda=L(x). Its exact logarithmic derivative has numerator 1-d^2(1-x)(1-y), which vanishes once and transversely. The m+n Jacobian consists of m-1 and n-1 negative transverse eigenvalues and a two-by-two collective block with determinant 1/((1-x)(1-y))-d^2, giving all equilibrium counts and local stability. At a star fold, y_c tends to zero and x_c tends to 1-d^-2, yielding lambda_c∼d^(2/(d+1))(1-d^-2)^(1-d)n^(-1/(d+1)). The 313 supplementary exact-rational/numerical checks in verify_bipartite.py passed. The finite checks are not substituted for the analytic all-size proof.

value.rationale: The full node-level opinion adoption equation was studied via a homogeneous approximation justified only for narrow degree distributions. Complete bipartite graphs form the simplest nontrivial two-degree family and include hub-dominated stars as a canonical stress test. The exact threshold and one-saddle/one-attractor classification identify a substantive topology-dependent onset law, especially lambda_c≈κ_d n^-1/(d+1) where the mean-degree reduction instead predicts an O(1) limit. The power and constant are precise enough to inform graph heterogeneity, nonlocal external influence and where approximation breaks, without overclaiming real-world or stochastic predictions.
